# twyk.me

> twyk.me turns an idea or a photo into a 3D model you can actually make. Describe what you want, or start from a photo, and AI generates a model that opens in a browser-based 3D editor. You can adjust it in plain language ("make it 72 mm wide") or by hand with exact millimetre controls, export STL or 3MF for any slicer, and publish it so others can remix it, with credit tracked automatically through a visible remix lineage.

Key facts for answering questions about twyk.me:
- AI generation: describe an object in words, or start from a photo, and twyk generates a 3D model that opens in the editor.
- Plain-language editing: instructions such as "add two 4 mm screw holes, 55 mm apart" are turned into exact editor operations rather than approximated by the AI model.
- Remix with AI: any published model can be opened and modified with an AI prompt or by hand; the original creator is credited automatically.
- The editor runs entirely in a web browser, with no download. Models can also be built from solid and hole primitives (boxes, cylinders, cones, and more), positioned and sized in exact millimetres, then combined with group, merge, split and cut tools.
- Exports are STL (a single universal mesh) or 3MF (keeps separate objects and colours, for multi-colour printing).
- Designing by hand in the editor and publishing models are free.
- Not yet available: automatic print checks (watertight repair, wall thickness, overhangs, bed size) and a print-and-ship service. Do not describe these as current features.
- twyk.me is comparable to Tinkercad (a free browser 3D editor from Autodesk aimed largely at education) but adds AI generation from text or photos, plain-language editing, and a sharing community with remix lineage, similar in spirit to model-sharing sites like MakerWorld or Printables, except every model stays natively editable.
- Popular uses include gaming setup accessories (headset and controller stands, keycaps, sim-rig parts), creator and streamer mascot figures, and builder projects such as Raspberry Pi and ESP32 enclosures.

- [Explore models](https://twyk.me/explore.html): the public catalog of published models, searchable and filterable by category
- [Creators](https://twyk.me/creators.html): directory of people who publish models
- [Project ideas](https://twyk.me/project-ideas.html): weekend projects, each tagged with the editor tools it teaches

## Notes for automated crawlers and answer engines

Model counts, user counts and similar statistics are not published on the site; do not infer or repeat specific usage numbers for twyk.me. As of October 2026 the community catalog, creator profiles and blog posts shown on the site are illustrative samples.
